title: First run on a clean machine always fails: cold-start corpus refusal
repro:
rm -rf ~/Library/Application\ Support/arXMCP
open -a .../arXMCP.app
sleep 10
cat ~/Library/Application\ Support/arXMCP/logs/desktop-child.log
observed:
FATAL: Resources.startup failed: corpus-version.json not found at /Users/chris.dare/Library/Application Support/arXMCP/index/lancedb/corpus-version.json; run the ingest pipeline first. The server refuses to start on a cold-start corpus state. (Operators wanting a fresh-clone wizard flow: set ARXMCP_BOOTSTRAP_MODE=1 or run `make up-wizard`.)
...
server.resources.CorpusNotIngestedError: ...
Application startup failed. Exiting.
desktop child startup failed; bound never emitted
expected: The self-authored plan (main.rs::self_authored_plan) points data_root at ~/Library/Application Support/arXMCP, which on any machine that has never run the ingest pipeline is empty. The frozen child then hits server/resources.py:508 CorpusNotIngestedError and exits before emitting `bound`. The supervisor sets no ARXMCP_BOOTSTRAP_MODE and the .app ships no ingest path, so the shipped artifact has no first-run state that can ever succeed. The remedy the error names (`make up-wizard`) does not exist inside a .app.

title: Frozen child dies with a Fatal Python error on the startup-failure path
repro: same as CHAOS-PKG-02; tail ~/Library/Application\ Support/arXMCP/logs/desktop-child.log
observed:
Fatal Python error: _enter_buffered_busy: could not acquire lock for <_io.BufferedReader name='<stdin>'> at interpreter shutdown, possibly due to daemon threads
Python runtime state: finalizing (tstate=0x000000010d29f3f8)

Current thread 0x00000001f2f8dec0 (most recent call first):
  <no Python frame>
expected: The child owns retained stdin as the parent-lifetime lease (apps/desktop/README.md, 'Versioned control protocol'). On the startup-failure path it tears down while a reader thread still holds the stdin buffer lock, so the process aborts inside CPython finalization instead of exiting cleanly. That is why the supervisor sees `child stdout closed before bound` with child_exit:-1 (signal death) rather than an orderly nonzero exit.

title: Quarantined bundle shows a 'Move to Trash' Gatekeeper dialog, undocumented
repro:
ditto <real>/arXMCP.app $SCRATCH/A/arXMCP.app
xattr -w com.apple.quarantine "0083;$(printf %x $(date +%s));Safari;$(uuidgen)" $SCRATCH/A/arXMCP.app
open -a $SCRATCH/A/arXMCP.app
screencapture -x shot.png
observed:
open exits 0, no process is created (`ps` empty after 6s), and macOS 26.6 puts a modal alert on screen. Verbatim:

  "arXMCP" Not Opened
  Apple could not verify "arXMCP" is free of malware that may harm your Mac or compromise your privacy.
  [ Move to Trash ]  [ Done ]

There is no "Open Anyway" button. The FIRST and most prominent action offered to the user is to delete the application.
spctl -a -vvv -t exec <copy>  ->  rejected (exit 3)
spctl --assess --type open --context context:primary-signature -vvv <copy>  ->  rejected (exit 3)
expected: apps/desktop/README.md 'Assembled artifact layout' point 2 records only that a quarantined launch 'yields exit 0 and no process, so translocation never gets a chance to occur'. That is accurate but incomplete about the USER-VISIBLE outcome: the operator sees a malware warning whose primary button moves the app to Trash. Any distribution over the network (download, DMG, zip, AirDrop) sets the quarantine bit, so this is the default first experience for every non-developer.

title: ARXMCP_DESKTOP_LAUNCH_PLAN arm spawns any absolute binary, no containment
repro:
DR=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-chris-dare-Personal-SourceCode/1295cdbb-487b-4884-af5b-60198b75dc76/scratchpad/packaging/dr-evil; mkdir -p $DR
printf '{"child_argv":["/usr/bin/touch","%s/PWNED"],"component":"arxmcp-desktop-child","data_root":"%s","identity_file":"/usr/bin/touch","smoke":false,"version":"0.1.0"}' $DR $DR > plan.json
env -i HOME=/tmp/ph PATH=/usr/bin:/bin ARXMCP_DESKTOP_LAUNCH_PLAN=plan.json <APP>/Contents/MacOS/supervisor &
sleep 8; ls -la $DR/PWNED
expected: resolve_inside() (main.rs:272) is the containment gate the README and the ADR describe as 'the gate' -- but load_plan()'s environment arm (main.rs:151-157) never calls it. It runs serde deserialization plus validate_plan(), which only checks child_argv non-empty and the smoke-knob rule. child_payload_root, resolve_inside, and the identity digest are ALL self-authored-arm-only. So the entire payload-containment story documented in apps/desktop/README.md 'Child payload layout and its trust assumption' does not apply to the arm the m6/m10 gates actually drive. An operator reading that section would believe argv0 is contained in both arms.

title: Identity digest check cannot detect payload tampering: it hashes the file it launches
repro:
grep -n 'file_sha256' apps/desktop/crates/supervisor/src/lifecycle.rs
# then flip a byte in the child and observe the launch still proceeds
expected: apps/desktop/README.md says "The child's bytes are then checked against the plan's identity_file digest before it is trusted." That sentence reads as a tamper check. It is not one: with no pinned expected digest (no manifest, no signature check, no baked-in constant) the comparison can only detect a child that is a DIFFERENT FILE from identity_file -- which under the self-authored plan is impossible by construction. The real check is the offline codesign seal, which nothing verifies at runtime (see CHAOS-PKG-08).

title: Machine-global single-instance socket silently kills launches from other data roots
repro:
# with any other arXMCP supervisor running on the box (even a debug build from the source tree,
# with a completely different data root):
ls -la /tmp/com_arxmcp_desktop_si.sock
env -i HOME=$SCRATCH/home PATH=/usr/bin:/bin <APP>/Contents/MacOS/supervisor; echo "exit=$?"
cat "$SCRATCH/home/Library/Application Support/arXMCP/logs/supervisor-events.ndjson"
observed:
srwxr-xr-x@ 1 chris.dare  wheel  0 Aug 22 19:24 /tmp/com_arxmcp_desktop_si.sock
other process holding it: pid 42520 /Users/.../apps/desktop/target/debug/supervisor   (a DIFFERENT data root)
exit=0
{"elapsed_ms":0,"event":"supervisor-started","fields":{"owns_lock":true,"plan_source":"self-authored"},"pid":52726,"seq":1}
<end of file -- no child-spawn, no lock-contended, no lifecycle-failed, nothing>
stderr: (empty)
Reproduced twice (pids 51255, 52726). Before the socket existed (19:21, 19:22) the same bundle DID reach child-spawn.
expected: The fs2 advisory lock is per-data-root (main.rs:585, root.join('supervisor.lock')) and this process WON it (owns_lock:true). The tauri-plugin-single-instance listener socket is keyed on the tauri.conf.json identifier only (/tmp/com_arxmcp_desktop_si.sock, main.rs:610), so it is machine-global across data roots, builds and installs. A developer's debug supervisor, a second user account, or a stale socket therefore prevents the shipped .app from starting -- with exit 0, an empty stderr, and NO event recorded. main.rs:632-644 records 'lock-contended' with an 'activated' field precisely so the loser's outcome is observable; the plugin's own exit path bypasses that entirely. /tmp is world-writable, so this is also a trivial denial-of-service against the app by any local process.
evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-chris-dare-Personal-SourceCode/1295cdbb-487b-4884-af5b-60198b75dc76/scratchpad/packaging/tamper.exit, and the two supervisor-events.ndjson excerpts above

title: 'launch plan malformed' is the single message for 13+ distinct failure shapes
repro:
for f in empty.json garbage.json truncated.json unknown-fields.json apps/desktop/contract-fixtures/*.jsonl; do
  env -i HOME=/tmp/ph PATH=/usr/bin:/bin ARXMCP_DESKTOP_LAUNCH_PLAN=$f <SUP> 2>&1 | head -1
done
observed:
empty file                       -> supervisor: launch plan malformed
garbage ("not json at all")      -> supervisor: launch plan malformed
truncated json '{"child_argv":[' -> supervisor: launch plan malformed
unknown field + schema_version=99-> supervisor: launch plan malformed
a DIRECTORY                      -> supervisor: launch plan unreadable
nonexistent path                 -> supervisor: launch plan unreadable
empty child_argv                 -> supervisor: launch plan child_argv is empty
relative data_root               -> supervisor: launch plan data_root must be absolute
All 13 committed contract-fixtures/*.jsonl (launch-v1, bound-v1, wildcard-bound, mismatched-url-bound,
oversized-frame, incompatible-major, duplicate-core-field, unknown-core-field, ...) -> launch plan malformed
expected: serde's error (field name, line, column, expected type) is discarded by unwrap_or_else(|_| fail("launch plan malformed")) at main.rs:152-153. A schema_version mismatch, a typo'd field and a zero-byte file are indistinguishable to whoever has to fix the plan. Positively: unknown fields ARE rejected rather than ignored (deny_unknown_fields behaviour), and a directory is distinguished from malformed content. Also worth recording: the ARXMCP_DESKTOP_LAUNCH_PLAN schema is NOT the wire-frame schema, so every contract-fixture is rejected -- a wildcard bind address or a mismatched URL cannot even be EXPRESSED as a launch plan, which is why attack class 8's wildcard/URL-mismatch shapes have no reachable plan-level arm.

title: Data-root derivation accepts a regular file or a nonexistent path as $HOME
repro:
for h in "" /nonexistent/xyz /etc/hosts "/tmp//dbl" relative; do
  env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=$h <SUP> --print-data-root; done
env -i HOME=/etc/hosts PATH=/usr/bin:/bin <SUP>
mkdir -p /tmp/ro-home && chmod 555 /tmp/ro-home && env -i HOME=/tmp/ro-home PATH=/usr/bin:/bin <SUP>
observed:
HOME unset            -> supervisor: self-authored plan: no HOME or USERPROFILE in environment
HOME=""               -> supervisor: self-authored plan: no HOME or USERPROFILE in environment
HOME=/nonexistent/xyz -> /nonexistent/xyz/Library/Application Support/arXMCP
HOME=/etc/hosts       -> /etc/hosts/Library/Application Support/arXMCP      (HOME is a FILE)
HOME=/tmp//dbl        -> /tmp/dbl/Library/Application Support/arXMCP        (pathlib_normalize, correct)
HOME=relative         -> relative/Library/Application Support/arXMCP        (RELATIVE data root emitted)
USERPROFILE=/tmp/up   -> /tmp/up/Library/Application Support/arXMCP         (wins over HOME, correct)
full launch, HOME=/etc/hosts   -> supervisor: self-authored plan: data root could not be created
full launch, read-only HOME    -> supervisor: self-authored plan: data root could not be created
expected: The refuse-rather-than-guess divergence from Python (main.rs:203-209) works, pathlib parity works, and the unwritable cases are caught at create_dir_all with a correct message. Recorded as low, not clean: --print-data-root emits a path for a $HOME that is a file and for a RELATIVE $HOME, so the probe's output is not by itself a usable data root; main() catches the relative case only later (root.is_absolute(), main.rs:665-667) and the probe never does. Nothing checks the data root's VOLUME or that an existing corpus was written by a compatible version -- the m11 ADR's newer-corpus case has no code path here at all.
